subject: chemistry
title: Titration calculations
key_idea: A titration finds the volumes of an acid and an alkali that react exactly. With one known concentration, calculate the moles of the known solution, use the equation ratio, then divide by the volume of the unknown solution.

blocks.text: (Higher tier, chemistry only) A titration measures the volume of one solution that reacts completely with a fixed volume of another. An indicator shows when the reaction is complete.

items.meaning: The volume of solution added from the burette to reach the end point.
The point where the indicator changes colour, showing the reaction is complete.
Titres that are very close together. The mean of these is used in the calculation.

items.text: Measure a fixed volume of one solution (for example 25.0 cm³ of alkali) into a conical flask.
Add a few drops of indicator.
Add the other solution (the acid) from the burette until the colour of the indicator changes.
Read the volume from the burette. Repeat until the results are concordant.

items: The titre is the volume added from the burette at the end point.
Use the mean of the concordant titres in the calculation.

blocks.text: Every titration calculation follows the same steps. Volumes in cm³ must be divided by 1000 to give dm³.

items.text: Work out the moles of the solution with the known concentration.
Use the balanced equation to find the moles of the unknown solution.
To give g/dm³, multiply the concentration in mol/dm³ by Mr.

blocks.text: 25.00 cm³ of dilute sulfuric acid reacts with 24.25 cm³ of 0.200 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the acid.

items.text: 1 mol H₂SO₄ reacts with 2 mol NaOH, so moles of H₂SO₄ = 0.00485 ÷ 2 = 0.002425 mol.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the concentration of sulfuric acid from a titration with sodium hydroxide.
diagram.question: 25.0 cm³ of sulfuric acid is neutralised by **{v}** cm³ of **{c}** mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid in mol/dm³.
working: Moles of H₂SO₄ = moles of NaOH ÷ 2, because the ratio is 1 : 2.

items: Moles = concentration × volume (dm³). Use it on the known solution first.
The equation ratio links the moles of the two solutions.
Concentration of the unknown = moles ÷ volume (dm³).

sections.heading: Concentration in g/dm³ and unknown volumes

blocks.text: (Higher tier, chemistry only) A titration can also give a concentration in g/dm³, or the volume of solution needed.

items: Find the concentration in mol/dm³ first.
Multiply by the relative formula mass. For sulfuric acid, 0.048 mol/dm³ × 98 = 4.70 g/dm³.

items.text: Moles of the known solution = concentration × volume (dm³).
Use the equation ratio to find the moles of the second solution.
Volume = moles ÷ concentration. Multiply by 1000 to give cm³.

blocks.text: Example: 25 cm³ of 0.12 mol/dm³ HCl needs 0.12 × 0.025 = 0.0030 mol NaOH (1 : 1). With 0.4 mol/dm³ NaOH, volume = 0.0030 ÷ 0.4 = 0.0075 dm³ = 7.5 cm³.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the volume of sodium hydroxide needed to neutralise hydrochloric acid.
diagram.question: 25.0 cm³ of **{a}** mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid is titrated with **{b}** mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide. HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Calculate the volume of sodium hydroxide needed, in cm³.
working: The ratio is 1 : 1, so moles of NaOH are the same.

items: Concentration in mol/dm³ × Mr = concentration in g/dm³.
Volume (dm³) = moles ÷ concentration. Multiply by 1000 to give cm³.

checks.q: In a titration, 20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide neutralises 25.0 cm³ of hydrochloric acid. HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the acid.
checks.a: Moles NaOH = 0.0200 × 0.100 = 0.00200 mol. The ratio is 1 : 1, so moles HCl = 0.00200 mol. Concentration = 0.00200 ÷ 0.0250 = 0.0800 mol/dm³.

checks.q: In a titration, the moles of acid are found to be half the moles of alkali. Where does this come from?
checks.a: The balanced equation. It shows 1 mole of the acid reacts with 2 moles of the alkali.

checks.q: A titration shows that a solution of sulfuric acid has a concentration of 0.048 mol/dm³. Mr of H₂SO₄ = 98. Calculate its concentration in g/dm³.

exam_phrases: add potassium hydroxide (solution) to the (conical) flask
until the colour (of the indicator) changes
read the volume from the burette

mistakes.wrong: Moles of HNO₃ = moles of Na₂CO₃, because both are in the equation.
mistakes.right: Use the ratio. Na₂CO₃ + 2HNO₃ means the moles of HNO₃ are 2 × the moles of Na₂CO₃. Use of an incorrect ratio loses the ratio mark.
Volume must be in dm³. Concentration = 0.0062 × 1000 ÷ 23.6 = 0.263 mol/dm³.
Divide the volume by 1000 first: 23.50 ÷ 1000 × 0.100 = 0.00235 mol.

worked_example.question:
A student does a titration using sodium carbonate solution and nitric acid.

The equation for the reaction is:

Na₂CO₃ + 2 HNO₃ → 2 NaNO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O

25.0 cm³ of 0.124 mol/dm³ sodium carbonate solution is neutralised by 23.6 cm³ of nitric acid.

Calculate the concentration of the nitric acid.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: Marks follow the steps: moles of the known solution, the 1 : 2 ratio, the concentration, then rounding.

exam_phrases: from reaction equation moles acid = ½ x moles alkali

mistakes.wrong: Moles of H₂SO₄ = 2 × moles of NaOH, giving 0.388 mol/dm³.
mistakes.right: The acid has half the moles of the alkali. Multiply by ½ (divide by 2), not by 2. The correct answer is 0.097 mol/dm³.

mistakes.wrong: Moles of H₂SO₄ = moles of NaOH, giving 0.194 mol/dm³.
mistakes.right: The equation is H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH. Use the ratio, so the moles of acid are half the moles of alkali.

worked_example.question:
In the titration, 25.00 cm³ of dilute sulfuric acid reacted with 24.25 cm³ of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide solution, NaOH.

H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O

Calculate the concentration of the dilute sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, in mol dm⁻³.
answer_points: From the equation, moles of acid = ½ × moles of alkali = 2.425 × 10⁻³ mol.
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 0.097 mol dm⁻³ with or without working scores all four marks.

exam_phrases: idea that moles of alkali = moles acid / 1:1 ratio

mistakes.wrong: The average titre is the mean of all four titres, including 26.4 and 25.8.
mistakes.right: Use only the titres the question tells you to use, here the concordant results 25.1 and 25.0. The average is 25.05 cm³.
0.048 is in mol/dm³. Multiply by Mr (98) to give g/dm³: 4.70 g/dm³.
Convert the volume to dm³ first. Moles of acid = 0.12 × 25.0 ÷ 1000 = 0.003 mol.

worked_example.question:
A student uses a potassium hydroxide solution with a concentration of 0.100 mol / dm³ to neutralise 25.0 cm³ of dilute sulfuric acid. The average titre of potassium hydroxide solution is 24.0 cm³.

This is the equation for the reaction.

2KOH + H₂SO₄ → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O

Calculate the concentration of sulfuric acid in g / dm³.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): H = 1.0   O = 16.0   S = 32.0
worked_example.tip: An answer of 4.7 g/dm³ scores all five marks. Find mol/dm³ first, then multiply by Mr.
